honestNegatives: ZERO failures are attributable to EVENT_LOGIC with committed signals proving it. Per the workstream mandate (do not tune event thresholds when perception is the real cause), NO event-logic fix was implemented and NO threshold was changed.

An earlier draft of the oracle classified wavea-faead-rally#1 as EVENT_LOGIC; probing the committed series showed it is a windowed artifact ending at 13708ms mid-swing, so the verdict was corrected to UNATTRIBUTABLE_HERE — the truncation check now runs before any logic verdict.
No paddle-speed series is committed for any oracle case, so paddle confirmation is structurally unavailable in every Linux replay (recorded per row, never guessed).
Held-out discipline: wm-dink-01 and afn-vic-rally1 rows cite only previously recorded Mac artifacts (cascade-1787971753680.json); no replay iteration or tuning was run against held-out material.
keyFinding: EVENT coverage failures are perception-side: 3/7 are wrist-signal quality (in-span smoothed peak below the 0.5 proposal floor on volleys/smash-adjacent events — short compact strokes barely move the wrist in normalized units), 1/7 is the known rally1 contact-anchor absence blocking selection despite a 0.9-overlap proposal, and 3/7 cannot be decided on Linux because the committed windowed artifacts truncate or omit the gold span. Tuning event thresholds would be treating the wrong layer.
whatRemainsBlocked: 3 UNATTRIBUTABLE_HERE events need Mac artifacts: datasets/paddle-bench/runs/wm-dink-01/{people.json,report.json} and datasets/paddle-bench/runs/wavea-faead-rally/people.json (full clip). Re-running the oracle on a Mac after pnpm lab:regen would decide them.

The 3 WRIST_SIGNAL_QUALITY events cannot be fixed in event logic without weakening the 0.5 proposal floor, which the mandate forbids without perception-side evidence; the decisive experiment is a paddle-speed (not wrist) series for those clips, which is not committed.
